pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/33886. We're concatenating all stdio chunks that are `string`, but we don't concatenate `Buffer` chunks. The addition of `Buffer` attachments seems to go back to https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/26391, but it's not sure if that was a necessary thing.

This PR fixes the issue by encoding all `Buffer` chunks, so they're concatenated together with the rest.
pr_comments: @yury-s you authored the addition of the code i'm removing here. Do we know if folks rely on having binary stdout chunks available as attachments? It's not obvious to me if this is a bug or a feature.

issue_context.title: [Bug]: Calling execSync() in test produces extra attachment
issue_context.body: ### Version 1.49.0 ### Steps to reproduce Follow the steps in README: https://github.com/vitalets/playwright-issues/tree/exec-sync-output The key point is calling `execSync()` in the test: ```ts test('my test', async ({}) => { console.log('foo'); execSync('echo bar', { stdio: 'inherit' }); console.log('baz'); }); ``` ### Expected behavior Single `stdout` attachment containing all outputs: ``` foo bar baz ``` ### Actual behavior There are two `stdout` attachments: 1. normal expandable `stdout` attachment: ``` foo baz ``` 2. binary `stdout` attachment Report: ### Additional context Also tried to call `execSync()` without `stdout: 'inherit'`, result is the same. ### Environment ```shell System: OS: macOS 13.6.9 CPU: (8) arm64 Apple M1 Memory: 56.22 MB / 16.00 GB Binaries: Node: 20.14.0 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.14.0/bin/node Yarn: 1.22.21 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.14.0/bin/yarn npm: 10.9.0 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.14.0/bin/npm pnpm: 7.27.1 - ~/Library/pnpm/pnpm IDEs: VSCode: 1.95.3 - /usr/local/bin/code Languages: Bash: 3.2.57 - /bin/bash npmPackages: @playwright/test: 1.49.0 => 1.49.0 ```
comments:
This seems to only happen with the HTML reporter. We concatenate all `text/plain` stdout chunks into one big attachment: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/a14d9750b314c26d72daa9f33598ad9d66d3e61c/packages/playwright/src/reporters/html.ts#L437-L447

The `execSync` output is of type `application/octet-stream` though, so it gets attached chunk-per-chunk. I'll see if it's safe for us to also concatenate those octet-stream chunks.

In the meantime, you can work around this by specifying `encoding: "utf-8" / "ascii"` in your `execSync` call.

review_comments: The only case that I can think of where it may be useful to see original binary output is a tool that produces e.g. an image and prints the bytes to stdout. And even in that case the users should store the output to an attachment manually rather than piping it to playwright's.
